name: Contact Physics
author: Kizi
description: What happens to a car in contact. Two models: Rigid body (mass, inertia, bounce, friction, rubbing tyres) or Classic (the 0.5 spin and tyre lift). Walls, aero loss, damage. AI driving: AI Driver Behaviour.

options.label: Physics: contact model
options.description: Rigid body = every touch calculated from both cars' mass, speed and contact point, with real bounce and grip. Classic = the 0.5 contact: set spin, twitch and tyre lift (cars fly more on tyre contact).

options.label: Crashes
options.description: Touches are always real. This sets how hard a crash plays out: how high cars fly, how far a spinning or broken car slides, the kick and spin after a rear break. Dramatic = a bit more than real. P = next level.

options.label: Classic: strength
options.description: How strong the Classic contact is: AI spin from hits, twitch, rear-hit spin, wheel-over-wheel lift (the old flying) and wheel-to-wheel push together. Wild = extreme push, can throw cars. Classic only.

options.label: Damage: rear suspension from wheel hits
options.description: When a car's front tyre hits a rear tyre at speed, that rear corner can break; the car then snaps round (see Crashes). A wing into a tyre breaks nothing. From 60 km/h and 0.3 m/s closing.

options.label: Damage: front suspension toughness
options.description: The game breaks front corners about as easily as rear ones. Tougher = half the game's front suspension damage, Much tougher = a quarter. Rear stays the game's. Every car, yours too.

options.label: Damage: loose wheels (no tethers)
options.description: A wheel torn off flies off as debris instead of hanging on the game's tethers, which drag the car to a dead stop. AI cars, or AI and your car. Off = the game's tethers.

options.label: Damage: tyre punctures
options.description: A hit at a tyre can puncture it: more likely the faster the cars and the harder the hit (from 40 km/h and 0.3 m/s closing, full at 150 km/h and 2 m/s). Uses the game's own puncture.

options.label: Damage: suspension after a jump
options.description: A car that flies (over a wheel, a kerb, another car) can land with damage. Damage = one corner badly damaged, it keeps going. Break = the corner can break (a wheel can come off).

options.label: Damage: energy-based wing damage
options.description: Hard car-to-car hits add front-wing damage that grows with the energy of the hit (speed squared), on top of the game's own. Rigid body only.

options.label: Damage: equal damage for AI cars
options.description: The game gives AI cars a different damage factor than your car. On = every AI car takes the same damage from a hit as your car would (wing, body parts, suspension).

options.label: Damage: your car too
options.description: On = your car gets the same as AI cars: punctures, rear suspension breaks, jump damage, the kick, launches and flights. Off = only AI cars.

options.label: Testing: log contacts
options.description: Writes every car-to-car touch to swofty\loader.log and shows crash events (breaks, launches, flights, slides) top-left for 6 s. Only for testing; leave off.
